::: {.callout-note}
## How to read this report
Every number comes from a script in `C_mutant_validation_DinMete/scripts/` (Steps 1–12 of
[our workflow](../C_mutant_validation_DinMete/project_outlines/PROJECT_WORKFLOW_mval.md)); each results folder
has a `figure_guide_mval.md` that says what each figure compares. Fold changes are
**log2, A − B**: `stp_vs_anc_at_TSB = −5.4` means **higher in anc**, lower in stp.
:::

# 1. Question and hypotheses

Stk1 (PknB, kinase) and Stp1 (phosphatase) are encoded in one *stp1–stk1* transcription
unit. The `stp` strain carries a transposon in *stp1* (NE1919, codon 189 of 247) upstream of
*stk1*, so it may also lack Stk1 (a polar effect).

- **H1** `stp` has reduced Stp1 **and** Stk1; `stk` has reduced Stk1.
- **H2** Some protein responses to *P. aeruginosa* spent medium (PASN) differ from the parent.
- **H3** Part of the `stp` pattern resembles `stk` (shared reduced-kinase component).

# 2. Design and data

*S. aureus* JE2 (`anc`), NE217 *stk1*::Tn (`stk`), NE1919 *stp1*::Tn (`stp`); TSB or
~15 h in 70 % TSB + 30 % cell-free, sterile-filtered PAO1 spent medium (`SN`, "PASN": only
secreted molecules plus partial nutrient depletion; never living *P. aeruginosa*).
n = 3 per group. Primary analysis: 18 samples (TSB, SN); all 27 (incl. SNpulse) inform the
variance. Total proteome: `r n_distinct(total$protein_key)` JE2 proteins; phosphoproteome
searched twice (STY, STYH).

# 3. Methods

| step | what | rule |
|---|---|---|
| model | limma, `~ 0 + group` (9 means), every contrast written as A − B | no reference level can flip a sign |
| hit | `treat()` (McCarthy & Smyth 2009) H0: \|log2FC\| ≤ 1; **BH-FDR < 0.05** within contrast | fixed 12 Nov, before results; no post-hoc fold-change filter |
| eligibility | tested only with ≥ 2 of 3 observed values in every group of the contrast | missing = not detected, never 0; no imputation |
| interaction | (mutant TSB − SN) − (anc TSB − SN) | > 0: SN response lower in the mutant |
| H3 similarity | correlation of `stp` and `stk` effects, corrected for the shared `anc` noise | method of moments, bootstrap CI |
| phospho | ≥ 2 of 3 per group, median per-sample localisation ≥ 0.75 (Olsen et al. 2006), S/T/Y; own BH family | site − protein in the same contrast, descriptive |
| pathways | rank test + limma `cameraPR` (Wu & Smyth 2012); robust = both FDR < 0.05 | background = proteins tested in the contrast |
| robustness | leave-one-sample-out, alternative thresholds, genome-position scan | sensitivity only |

Software: R, limma (Ritchie et al. 2015), tidyverse; versions in section 10.

**Hand check of one number** (workflow Step 12): the Stk1 difference `stp_vs_anc_at_TSB`
recomputed from the per-sample values, next to the model estimate.

```{r hand-check}
ab <- read_abundances("total") |> keep_je2() |> filter(locus_tag == "B7H15_06355", group %in% c("stp_TSB", "anc_TSB"))
by_hand <- ab |> group_by(group) |> summarise(mean = mean(normalized_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), n = sum(!is.na(normalized_abundance)))
model <- total |> filter(locus_tag == "B7H15_06355", contrast == "stp_vs_anc_at_TSB")
kable(by_hand, digits = 2)
stopifnot(abs((by_hand$mean[by_hand$group == "stp_TSB"] - by_hand$mean[by_hand$group == "anc_TSB"]) - model$diff) < 1e-8)
explain_contrast("stp_vs_anc_at_TSB")
```

Mean of `stp_TSB` minus mean of `anc_TSB` = **`r round(model$diff, 2)`** = the model
estimate (SE `r round(model$std.error, 2)`, FDR `r signif(model$FDR, 2)`): Stk1 is
**higher in anc**, about `r round(2^-model$diff)`-fold.

# 4. H1: what do the mutants lack?

```{r fig1, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
include_graphics(file.path(res_dir, "step12_poster/fig1_h1_enzymes_mval.png"))
```

```{r h1-table, echo=FALSE}
kable(rd("step03_validation/evidence_table_mval.csv"),
      caption = "Step 3 evidence table (detections TSB/SNpulse/SN of 3 each; supplied lm_impute estimates are presence/absence evidence where lod_imputed).")
```

- **Stk1:** not detected in `stk` in TSB or SN (0/6). In `stp` it is ~43-fold lower in TSB
  (estimate above) and resting on 1–2 peptides (29–32 in `anc`), and not detected in SN.
  The site T164 of Stk1 falls with the protein (Step 9).
- **Stp1:** 0–2 peptides in `stp` vs 9–15 in `anc`. The abundance values that remain are
  erratic, so the **size** of the loss cannot be estimated. Stp1 is unchanged in `stk`.
- **Insertion control:** ErmB (transposon marker) in 18/18 mutant samples, 0/9 `anc`
  (Step 4b, separate FragPipe search incl. transposon proteins).
- Neighbours of *stp1/stk1* are unchanged (Step 4). The pattern fits a polar insertion;
  protein data cannot exclude reduced stability, regulation or a secondary mutation.

# 5. H2: altered responses to PASN

```{r fig2, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
include_graphics(file.path(res_dir, "step12_poster/fig2_h2_responses_mval.png"))
```

```{r h2-table, echo=FALSE}
stab <- rd("step11_robustness/loso_hit_stability_mval.csv")
stab |> filter(str_starts(contrast, "interaction")) |>
  transmute(contrast, protein = coalesce(gene, locus_tag), diff = round(diff, 2), FDR = signif(FDR, 2),
            `in words` = if_else(diff > 0, "SN response lower in first strain", "SN response higher in first strain"),
            `leave-one-out` = paste0(refits_still_hit, "/18"),
            `in shifted genomic block` = !is.na(in_own_block)) |>
  kable(caption = "All formal interaction hits (Step 6/7) with their Step 11 stability. First strain = the mutant named first in the contrast.")
```

Both mutants keep most of the PASN response (r = 0.85 `stk`, 0.86 `stp` against `anc`).
Only 5 of 1,882 (`stk`) and 1 of 1,931 (`stp`) tested proteins change their response.
Raw values (Step 6) show that argF and B7H15_14515 are mainly a TSB baseline difference in
`stk`, arcA and kdpD differ in both media, and only rbsD is mainly an SN difference. The
single `stp` hit, ilvA, is fragile (9/18 refits) and probably shared with `stk` (one `stk_SN`
replicate only). A lower threshold (1.5-fold) triples the lists but keeps the shape:
`stk` 15 vs `stp` 5 (Step 11).

**kdpD is not an `stk`-specific response.** The peptide check of Step 6d shows that the
whole *kdp* system is switched off in PASN in **all three** strains: only ~5 % of the KdpD
peptide observations seen in TSB remain (rank 9 of 1,121 well-covered proteins, at equal
sequencing depth), so each SN protein value rests on 0–3 peptides instead of 12–27. The
`stk`-specific interaction is therefore most likely an artefact of summarising very few
peptides; it also survives only 14 of 18 leave-one-out refits and lies in a genomic block
that shifts in `stk` (section 8). The robust `stk` result is the arc operon (arcA + argF).

# 6. H3: does stp look like stk?

```{r fig3, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
include_graphics(file.path(res_dir, "step12_poster/fig3_h3_shared_distinct_mval.png"))
```

```{r h3-table, echo=FALSE}
rd("step07_shared_distinct/similarity_stats_mval.csv") |>
  transmute(layer, proteins = n, `observed r` = round(r, 2), `noise-only r` = round(r_noise_only, 2),
            `noise-corrected r` = round(r_true_corrected, 2),
            `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", r_true_low, r_true_high),
            `split-reference r (lower bound)` = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", r_split_reference_min, r_split_reference_max)) |>
  kable(caption = "Similarity of the stp and stk effects (Step 7).")
```

Both axes subtract the same `anc` means, so noise alone gives r ≈ 0.50. After removing that
part, the true effects correlate moderately (0.37–0.38): clearly above 0, far below 1.
Only 3 proteins are hits in both mutants (same direction). 20 (TSB) + 4 (response) proteins
differ directly; 6 of the 20 lie in genomic blocks that shift as a unit (section 8). At
pathway level `stp` shares the peptidoglycan-synthesis and cytolysis shifts of `stk`, not the
SigB/*mazEF* or ATP-synthase shifts (Step 10).

# 7. Phosphorylation (supporting layer)

```{r phospho, echo=FALSE}
rd("step08_phospho_coverage/phospho_hit_counts_mval.csv") |> filter(search == "STY") |>
  select(contrast, supported_sites, our_hits_up, our_hits_down, supplied_screen_hits_all_sites) |>
  kable(caption = "Step 8 (STY search): sites usable per contrast and site hits (treat lfc = 1, our BH-FDR < 0.05). Supplied screen for comparison only.")
```

Only 91–184 of 3,774 sites per contrast are measured often and localised well enough; none
responds differently to PASN in a mutant. Of 62 site hits (mostly TSB vs SN), 17 follow
their protein, 40 change more than their protein (Step 9; the adjusted effect is descriptive,
assuming independent layers). Genotype examples: deoB T85 lower in `stk` (TSB, protein
unchanged), pyk T537 higher in `stp`, Stk1 T164 lower in `stp` with the protein.

```{r fig-phospho, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
include_graphics(file.path(res_dir, "step09_site_vs_protein/fig_paired_layers_mval.png"))
```

# 8. Pathway level and genome position

```{r fig4, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
include_graphics(file.path(res_dir, "step12_poster/fig4_pathways_genome_mval.png"))
```

```{r blocks, echo=FALSE}
rd("step11_robustness/genome_top_windows_mval.csv") |>
  mutate(p_familywise = if_else(p_familywise == 0, "< 0.001", as.character(round(p_familywise, 3)))) |>
  kable(caption = "Most extreme 10-protein window per contrast (Step 11; threshold = genome-wide 5 %, 1000 permutations).")
```

Many functional terms shift in both mutants, `stp` as many as `stk` in TSB and SN; `stk` has
more only in the response. "Stk1 broadly involved" is therefore **not** specific to the kinase
mutant. Two genomic blocks change as a unit:

- **`stk`, B7H15_11470–11590** (SigB operon, *mazEF*, *alr1*, *acpS*, *kdpCBA/DE*, *murF*,
  *ddl*): +1.5 log2, the top window in the genome. Unrelated neighbours rising ~2-fold
  together fit a copy-number change in this strain; regional regulation is the alternative.
- **`stp`, B7H15_10910–11150, a prophage:** −2.1 log2 in TSB; it also drives the most
  extreme windows of both interaction contrasts.

# 9. Answers, limitations and follow-up

| | answer | status (Step 11) |
|---|---|---|
| **H1** | `stp` lacks most Stk1 (~43-fold) as well as Stp1; `stk` lacks Stk1 | **supported**; polar mechanism consistent, not proven |
| **H2** | Few altered PASN responses (5 `stk`, 1 `stp`); the response is largely intact | **supported, small**; 2 `stk` hits fully robust, `stp` hit fragile |
| **H3** | A moderate shared component (r ≈ 0.37) plus clear differences | **partly supported (tentative)** |

**Limitations.** n = 3 (non-significance is weak evidence of no effect); no clean deletions
or complemented strains; the `stp` strain is a phosphatase mutant with strongly reduced kinase,
not a phosphatase-only mutant; phosphosite coverage is sparse; two genomic blocks may reflect
strain differences; PASN mixes secreted molecules and nutrient depletion; total-proteome run
order was blocked by group (drift cannot be separated from group).

**Follow-up proposal (future experiments).** (1) Sequence the three strains or run qPCR on
the *stk* block (B7H15_11465–11700) and the prophage region. (2) Measure *stp1*/*stk1*
transcripts in `stp` to test polarity. (3) Compare clean Δ*stp1* (keeping Stk1), Δ*stk1* and
a verified double deletion with complemented strains under PASN.
